summary.tldr: Amends the National Capital Act to set Gatineau Park boundaries, protect its ecological integrity, and add rules for land use, consultation, and fees.
what_it_does: Establishes Gatineau Park as a defined area in a new schedule, and sets out rules for enlarging it but not shrinking it, except in a court title finding case.
Requires the National Capital Commission to put ecological integrity first when managing the park, and to prepare and update a Gatineau Park Master Plan.
Prohibits disposing of public lands in the park, with limited exceptions for Algonquin Anishinabeg services and public health care or infrastructure.
Requires the Commission to consult the Algonquin Anishinabeg Nation and neighbouring municipalities, and to report that it has considered their recommendations.
Allows the Commission to negotiate right of first refusal agreements with private landowners, so it can buy property before it is sold.
Authorises regulations on park activities, resource use, fees, and penalties, and lets the Commission rely more on Algonquin Anishinabeg businesses and workers for maintenance and conservation.
summary.background: The bill amends the National Capital Act. It adds a new schedule that describes Gatineau Park boundaries and renumbers the existing schedule as Schedule 1.
